paras: The Troy depot crowd incident was a confrontation at the railway depot in Troy, Pennsylvania, about August 25, 1882, in which a crowd shouted threats at a Black man boarding a night train with a white woman. Told that the pair were eloping, the crowd cried "Hang the man," and the man left the train; no one was reported hurt.

According to the woman, her husband farmed near Sullivan, Tioga County, and the Black man had worked on the place for about a year. She said she had left her husband about three weeks before, that there had been "a good deal of talk" about her and the man, and that she had sent him word not to take her train. The first reports said instead that she had deserted a husband and children.

The two boarded the midnight express on the Northern Central Railway at Troy, and passengers were told they were "an eloping couple." A large crowd in the depot then cried "Put her off" and "Hang the man." According to the Evening Critic, the man said as he left that he feared harm and that the woman had wanted him to run away with her. She stayed aboard, bound for Washington, but stopped in Baltimore.

On September 4 she waited in the Baltimore and Potomac depot in Washington, gave her name as Wilson, and said she had been visiting acquaintances at Bealton, Virginia. The Evening Star wrote that she admitted to others that the man had bought two tickets for Bealton; that night she took the train for Troy.

The Evening Critic and the Evening Star of Washington ran the same paragraph on September 1 under the heading "An Elopement and Excitement," treating the crowd's cries as color in an elopement story. The Star's follow-up of September 5, headed "The Troy, Pa., Miscegenation Elopement," dwelt on the woman's dress and "suspicious facts in the case."
The September 1 paragraph reported threats and an elopement, but the woman told the Star that the story was not correct "in all particulars" and scoffed at the idea of threats.

reader.title: Troy depot crowd incident
bases: A crowd in the Troy depot shouted 'Hang the man' at a Black man travelling with a white woman and he left the train; no one was reported harmed (A1, A2).
A large crowd cried 'Hang the man' over a reported interracial elopement, but the man left the train and no killing or assault is reported (A1, A2); the woman later scoffed at the threats (A3).
The two Sept. 1 Washington paragraphs share one text, apparently from the Baltimore Sun (A1, A2); the woman interviewed on Sept. 4 denied the story and scoffed at the idea of threats (A3).

accounts.label: Wire paragraph (via Baltimore Sun)
accounts.gist: A large crowd at the Troy depot, told the pair were eloping, cried 'Put her off' and 'Hang the man,' and the Black man left the train while the woman went on to Baltimore.

accounts.label: The woman's account
accounts.gist: She denied eloping or travelling with the man, scoffed at the threats, and said she had warned him by message not to take the same train after local talk about them.

accounts.label: Evening Star reporter
accounts.gist: The reporter pressed her that the man bought the tickets and wrote that she admitted to others he bought two tickets for Bealton in Washington.

framing.detail: Both Washington evening papers ran the same short paragraph headed 'An Elopement and Excitement' without comment on the crowd.

The Star's follow-up, 'The Troy, Pa., Miscegenation Elopement', centred on the woman's appearance and 'suspicious facts', repeated a passenger's slur, and treated the crowd's threats only through her denial.

versions.value: Crowd cried 'Hang the man'; the pair were an eloping couple
Woman denied eloping and scoffed at the idea of threats

conflicts.note: The woman's denial is her own account; the reporter recorded that she admitted to others the man bought two tickets for Bealton.

record_check.dossier: Threat by a depot crowd with no assault; intimidation, and the woman disputed the threats
Articles say only 'Troy, Pa.'; the couple came from Sullivan, Tioga County
Three white articles in two Washington papers, Sept. 1 and Sept. 5
The woman denied the elopement and scoffed at the threats

info: About Friday, August 25, 1882 ('a week ago' from Sept. 1; the woman said she left Troy 'on Friday week'), at the midnight express
Depot at Troy, Pa., Northern Central Railway
An unnamed Black man, described as a farmhand on the woman's husband's farm near Sullivan, Tioga County; no one hurt
Said to be eloping with a married white woman
A 'large crowd' in the depot, unnamed
The woman travelled on to Baltimore and Washington, went to Bealton, Va., and on Sept. 4 took a train back toward Troy
